definitions.explanation: Losing a physical item, especially important documents, valuables, or personal belongings. More formal than simply saying something was lost.

examples.japanese: パスポートを{紛失|ふんしつ}した。
{鍵|かぎ}の{紛失|ふんしつ}を{届|とど}け{出|で}た。
examples.english: I reported the loss of my key.

examples.japanese: {書類|しょるい}を{紛失|ふんしつ}した{場合|ばあい}は、{速|すみ}やかに{担当者|たんとうしゃ}に{連絡|れんらく}してください。
examples.english: If you lose any documents, please contact the person in charge immediately.

notes:
{紛失|ふんしつ} is a formal noun that also functions as a suru-verb ({紛失|ふんしつ}する). It is the standard formal word for losing a physical item.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- パスポートを{紛失|ふんしつ}する (to lose one's passport)
- {紛失届|ふんしつとどけ} (a lost item report)
- {紛失|ふんしつ}{届|とどけ}を{出|だ}す (to file a lost item report)
- {紛失|ふんしつ}{防止|ぼうし} (loss prevention)

RELATED WORDS:
{なくす} is the everyday word for losing something. {紛失|ふんしつ} is more formal and is used in official reports, announcements, and business contexts. {遺失|いしつ} (loss of property) is even more formal and is used in legal contexts — {遺失物|いしつぶつ} means "lost property."
